complexity_ledger.narrative: CL-01, wave 1, first and alone. THE MODEL DID NOT MOVE AND WAS NOT MEANT TO. Ticket `current/` equals `desired/`; every figure the machine-checked core above reports is inherited from RM-05 and says nothing about this ticket. What moved is the eval harness, which is out of model by design. WHAT WAS BROKEN, reproduced on the real record at 400c296 before anything was written. (1) `SUPPORTED_VERSIONS = (1,2,3,4)` was an argparse `choices` literal, so an adopter following the card's own change rule got `error: invalid choice: '5'` and had to edit our Python. (2) Dropping the flag stamped `VERSION` -- 4 -- onto cards scaffolded from a version 5 rubric, and `check` reported 0 problems, exit 0. (3) Rewriting a dimension caveat in an adopter's own words took `serve` from 6,318 bytes to 6,092 -- the caveat vanished -- with `anchors_digest` byte-identical and nothing reporting it. (4) `audit` exited on a `FileNotFoundError` traceback for anyone who installed `score_tools.py` alone, and `REPO_ROOT = HERE.parents[3]` was an install-depth literal. WHAT SHIPS. The version population is `SUPPORTED_VERSIONS` UNION what the card file's `### Version history` declares, so a bump is two edits to the card and none to any Python; the default is the version the card declares, never a constant here; a version the card does not declare is refused by name with the two edits that would make it legal. The caveat parse is positional and drops nothing. ` beside the anchors digest -- rather than a widened first one, because the first column's claim (versions 1-3 declare the same anchors digest: the bar did not move) is TRUE and a widened digest would make it false. The optional siblings are optional and say so by name. `references/adopting_the_scorecard.md` is the how. THE CONSTRAINT, MEASURED BOTH SIDES. `serve | wc -c` is 6,319 at 400c296 and 6,319 at this tip; 9 anchor rungs both; `serve --digest-only` is `sha256:a213a36770ccab09` both; versions 1/2/3 are 4,488 / 5,229 / 5,586 both. Byte-identical at every version, so no sealed card's `served_digest` or `digest` is re-based and `check specs/results/scorecards` reports the same 330 problems before and after. Nothing was added to the served surface: every addition lives in ` a new reference page, all outside what `serve` renders. No anchor was added. No gate was added to any product surface. AND THE BUDGET IN THE PLAN DOES NOT REPRODUCE, filed as `CL-01-DF-01`. Four documents say the served surface is 6,409 bytes; RM-05's own REPRODUCE section prints the command, and run as written it gives 6,319 -- with the same method at 19c5c7b giving 8,306 against the published 8,396, exactly 90 low at both ends. `serve` writes 92 bytes of provenance to stderr. The direction stands (-23.9% against the published -23.7%) and the rung and line counts reproduce exactly; the absolute constant every ticket in this epic is budgeted against does not. SUITE, WITH TREES. 2 failed / 1469 passed at 400c296 in a clean checkout at /Users/hayde/IdeaProjects/wt-epic-close-the-loop; 2 failed / 1477 passed at this tip. The numerator rose by 8 and the denominator did not fall -- 8 new tests, nothing deleted, weakened or skipped, and all 8 fail against the parent source. The two reds are the inherited ones and neither was touched.

refinement.detail: Searched, found none, and the reason is that CL-01 changes no model. The ticket's declared `model_delta_expectation` is `none expected` and this ticket's `current/` and `desired/` are byte-identical (`diff -rq` clean), so `TlaSpecDevCli.tla` at this tip is `TlaSpecDevCli.tla` at 400c296. The figures measured above -- 9 variables, 17 actions, bound 1,111,320 over 7 of 9 resolved variables, delta direction ZERO against RM-05 -- are inherited unchanged and describe the predecessor's model rather than this ticket's work. The over-cap bound is RM-05's and is untouched here. The implementation lives entirely outside the model surface, in `examples/validation/scorecards/` and `references/`, which the plan's `representation_scope` keeps out of model deliberately: the eval harness is not program surface. There is no model refinement to search for, and inventing one to fill this field would be the move MF-020 forbids. WHAT WAS SEARCHED ON THE HARNESS, since that is where the change is. Three reductions were considered and one was taken. (a) Widening `anchors_digest` to cover the served bytes would be one digest instead of two -- REJECTED, because it falsifies the version 1-3 row, whose claim is that the bar held still while those versions served 4,487, 5,228 and 5,585 different bytes. (b) Deriving the scored dimension set from the card file above version 4, folding `RETIRED_AT` and `TOP_SCORE_V4` into the parse -- NOT TAKEN, filed as `CL-01-DF-02`; it binds what CL-04 may conclude about portability and the constants it would move are the ones 73 sealed cards are checked by under `R-H4`. (c) Replacing the caveat regex with a positional rule -- TAKEN. The old `\n\n(\*\*[A-Z].+?)\Z` returned the empty string for anything it did not recognise; the caveat is now whatever follows the last anchor, which is fewer conditions and no silent branch.

goals.expected_effect: A stranger can run the change rule, and silent failure becomes loud.

ticket.objective: FIRST AND ALONE -- nothing else in the portability argument matters until this works. SUPPORTED_VERSIONS = (1,2,3,4) is a literal in our source, so an adopter bumping to 5 must edit our code, AND IT FAILS SILENTLY: a v5 card is stamped version 4 and check reports 0 problems. Worse, THE SEAL DOES NOT SEAL WHAT A JUDGE READS -- rewriting a caveat deletes it from the served bytes while anchors_digest stays byte-identical. Fix SUPPORTED_VERSIONS, the caveat parse and the audit bootstrap so a bump needs no source edit; make an unsupported version REFUSED LOUDLY with the v5 case as the demonstrated failing input; make the seal cover the served bytes, saying whether the digest is widened or a second seal is added and why; and ship a SHORT adopter-facing page saying HOW, since portable_scorecard.md already says WHAT.
ticket.title: Make the card's change rule runnable by a stranger, and make it fail loudly
